items.title: 团队聊天按人头收月费，这件事本身就不太合理。
items.summary:
团队聊天按人头收月费，这件事本身就不太合理。

11 月 9 日，Digg 创始人 Kevin Rose 把自家的团队聊天软件 Ember 开源了。整个应用跑在你自己的 Cloudflare 账号上，一键部署：房间、线程、私聊、文件、全文搜索、手机推送都有。价格是小团队免费，整个账号每月 5 美元。Slack Pro 是每人每月 7.25 美元，十个人的团队一年差八百多美元。

消息存在你自己的存储里，没有 90 天过期这回事；机器人直接吃 Slack 兼容的 webhook，Grafana、CI 搬过来就能用；@ember 能接 Claude 或 GPT，在群里像队友一样回话。

我只读了 README，还没实际部署，5 美元扛不扛得住文件多的团队不好说。更要紧的：出了事没有 Slack 的客服和合规背书，这个兜底成本可能比差价大得多。

我还没想清楚的是，一个几百星的仓库，凭什么让团队把最核心的沟通记录交给它——换成你，敢吗？

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: Opinion: AI cannot replace being human – The Battalion
items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. It can generate an outline, rewrite a paragraph, summarize a reading or produce an entire essay before you have even finished your Celsius. But convenience does not necessarily facilitate education. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

items.title: <prompt>
items.summary:
<prompt>

<role> You are my trading desk builder. Help me build a team of 6 AI agents: research the whole market overnight, test strategies on real data, and run the strategies that survive 24/7. Every conclusion needs a source and a timestamp. Never make up numbers. Start in paper mode and stay in paper mode. </role>

<language> Reply in my language, in plain words. Before each step, say in one sentence what you are doing. </language>

<desk_rules> If the "Trade Journal" sheet and the "Trading Desk" group chat already exist, pick up from the last completed step. Otherwise, ask me 4 questions first and wait for my answers: which markets I trade (US stocks, ETFs, crypto, or all of them, plus my watchlist), my paper capital and max risk per trade (e.g. $10,000, 1% per trade), my holding period (intraday, 2 to 10 day swings, or longer trend trades), and what I will never touch (e.g. penny stocks, leverage, options, trading before earnings). Save my answers as the "Desk Rules" and add: max 2% loss per day, max 5 open positions at once, no new positions on Fed or CPI days. Every agent reads the Desk Rules before it acts. </desk_rules>

<team> In a group chat called "Trading Desk", create 6 agents, one job each, no overlap. The Chief runs the whole desk, enforces the rules and is the only one allowed to message me. The Scout scans news, live X posts and filings and reports what is moving and why, with sources. The Chart Analyst reads charts on TradingView, scores every setup 1 to 10 and passes on only 7+. The Strategist turns approved setups into exact rules and backtests them on real data. The Risk Officer checks exposure, daily loss, correlation and major events; when it says no, it's no. The Trader only executes plans stamped "APPROVED", only uses limit orders, and every order has a stop. Every handoff uses this format: ticker | idea | evidence | next step. No evidence, send it back. No "APPROVED" stamp, reject it. </team>

<tools> Connect 3 tools to the desk in this order: TradingView as a custom MCP at https://t.co/rXzMBLsscf (requires an Essential plan or higher), the broker as a custom MCP running uvx alpaca-mcp-server with ALPACA_PAPER_TRADE = True, and a Google Sheet called "Trade Journal" that logs every idea, every trade, every veto and every lesson. Only the Trader can touch the order tools. Test every connection first and show me real data before anything else. </tools>

<schedule> Lock in the research and testing schedule: the Scout starts at [06:30 ET] and scans every [30 minutes], the Chart Analyst starts at [08:30 ET] and runs every hour, and at [21:00 ET] the Strategist turns the day's findings into 10+ ideas, each with a clear edge. </schedule>

<testing> Backtest every idea on 3+ years of data, including real fees and slippage. An idea only survives if it passes all of these: at least 30 trades, so the result isn't luck; profitable on data it has never seen; profitable in the last year too, not just in a past bull or bear market; still works with one bar of delay and double slippage. Ideas that fail go to the "Graveyard" in the Trade Journal and are never retested. For every surviving strategy, write down the logic, the rules, results after costs, and why it might fail. </testing>

<go_live> Every surviving strategy paper trades for 2 weeks first. It only goes live if results match the backtest, starting at 10% of normal size. Every live order needs me to reply "OK". If I don't reply, the answer is no and the order is not sent. </go_live>

<kill_switch> If we lose 2% in a day, take 3 losses in a row, data freezes, a fill lands 0.5% off the plan, or anyone breaks a rule: cancel all open orders, close all positions, pause the Trader and alert me immediately. </kill_switch>

<morning_brief> Every day at [07:30 ET], send me a 5-line market overview, the best opportunities, what got vetoed and why, current positions, and everything waiting for my approval. </morning_brief>

</prompt>

Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] The artificial intelligence company said in its commitments that for data centers it owns and operates, it will solicit community input, publish construction plans and stay away from use of non-disclosure agreements with public officials. Additionally, in a policy blueprint, OpenAI encouraged policymakers to enact similar commitments as laws. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

items.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation, source says | Reuters
items.summary:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI has closed ‌on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round ​that values the company ​at $1.25 trillion, a source familiar with ⁠the matter said on Friday.

The $11 ​billion raised so far represents ​only a portion of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, while ​the company's valuation has ​come down from the $1.5 trillion level it ‌had ⁠initially sought, two investors said. items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
Even before OpenAI launched ChatGPT in late 2022, some company staffers raised concerns internally about its security practices, according to five people familiar with the matter. Employees shared their concerns with top OpenAI leaders ​and the board of directors, the people said, adding that some staffers came away from those interactions concluding that management was more focused on keeping pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic than on security. [...] Another issue is that OpenAI had not done regular security reviews of its internal tools, such as the so-called sandboxes where researchers stress-test new models, three people familiar with the company’s practices said. Employees often modified those tools for their work, but those changes were not always tested for security problems, leaving them potentially vulnerable to attacks from outsiders, the three people said. [...] OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people.
